study.question: Does adding g1-style evolving task-query event reads and terminal target-field matching to the intact g0 representation improve validation macro AUC above both frozen source bests, especially g0 at 0.8301982212762624, and is any added value attributable to adaptive same-field routing rather than the extra retrieval branch alone? Observed source evidence: DIN 0.8099233880793816, g0 0.8301982212762624, g1 0.8192325306335276. g0 beats g1 on every full-validation task, but the architectures differ. g0 empty-history macro AUC is 0.7248235765734043 versus DIN 0.7268428930232654 and g1 0.7307799953736445, with only 13 buy positives among 6444 examples; this exploratory slice is not evidence of a stable mechanism failure. g0 history>64 macro AUC is 0.8528771120550432 versus g1 0.8417448005421858. Only these three committed trajectories are locally available; their unimported ancestors, failures and abandoned branches cannot be treated as local evidence.
study.hypothesis: Implementation inspection shows that g0 compresses events into shared target-weighted relation/time and feedback memories before its one JointBlock; no final task-conditioned query returns to the uncompressed event stream. The committed g1 retains read-only event keys for two evolving-query reads and task-specific terminal low-rank value pooling with an adaptive bounded exact-match prior. A task query conditioned on the stronger g0 representation may retrieve complementary event evidence lost by shared signed-weight summaries. Preserve the complete g0 model and add a zero-start residual from this g1-inspired branch to each tower's existing pooled-value input. Adaptive routing should outperform both frozen sources and the no-prior/uniform/rotated active controls if query-dependent same-field alignment adds utility in this tested implementation. This is a prospective compatibility hypothesis, not an established mechanism or verified novelty claim.

study.proposed_difference: Append TerminalRetrieval only after g0 reset/initialization inside torch.random.fork_rng(devices=[]). It seeds four task states from the mean of g0 valid final tokens plus four learned identities, executes two dynamic shared-weight history reads with task mixing, then pools 112-wide item/action values with the same Q/K and a five-field terminal prior. Reconstruct through rank 32 and nonaffine normalization, then use a zero-initialized 112x112 output to add a per-task residual to g0's existing pooled-value input; tower dimensions remain unchanged. All modules have identical shapes and initialization across adaptive/none/uniform/rotated arms, and all three prior tensors are computed in each arm. Cyclic rotation changes the field-weight-to-match-channel assignment without changing values, masks or matches. No internal match bias or reverse event write is added. Padded IDs are sanitized by inherited g0 code, target action stays zero, matching rejects zero/padding IDs, all-empty reads have a zero null, and zero-history updates are exactly masked to zero. Source AST comparisons confirm unchanged FeedbackMemory, JointBlock and all g0 representation helpers; host forward/backward gates remain pending.
predictions: Primary: hybrid_adaptive will exceed g0 0.8301982212762624 and g1 0.8192325306335276 on all-sample validation macro AUC; report macro Logloss plus signed AUC/Logloss changes for each of the four tasks against DIN and both sources, with no undeclared task veto.

Adaptive-specific support requires hybrid_adaptive > hybrid_none and hybrid_uniform. Adaptive > hybrid_rotated would further support alignment of selected field weights to their own match channels; equal adaptive/rotated performance leaves that attribution unresolved.

Any first-seed advantage is preliminary. Seek at least three host-authorized paired seeds for selected arm, g0 and the closest active control; use paired user-cluster bootstrap if supported by the authorized host interface, without treating impressions as independent.

Exploratory slices use only predeclared history bins empty/1-16/17-64/>64 and positive-ID match occupancy absent/one/multiple fields. Report sample and per-task positive/negative counts, missing intervals and insufficient support; do not choose slice bins from validation outcomes. The new branch produces no direct evidence on empty histories.

All four arms should have the same parameter count. Measure training seconds, complete-unit wall seconds, inference latency/throughput and peak memory; runtime equality is not assumed.
falsifiers: Failure to exceed the stronger frozen g0 source is evidence against added predictive utility for this implementation, even if it exceeds g1 or DIN; it does not refute all possible representation/interaction combinations.

If no-prior or uniform retrieval reproduces the adaptive gain, reject the adaptive-routing explanation; attribute the result to a broader retrieval/capacity/optimization alternative pending further controls.
If cyclic rotation matches adaptive, do not claim identified field alignment. If repeat gains vanish or reverse, treat first-seed selection as unstable.
If measured cost is dominated at comparable quality by a source or active control, do not claim efficiency or justified added cost. AUC gain alone does not prove an equal-compute advantage.

Host initialization parity failure, unavailable-input dependence, nonfinite forward/loss/gradients, padding sensitivity, nonzero empty-history residual, or a hard resource violation invalidates that implementation before interpreting metrics.
